content.user_title: Improve UI Motion and Interaction Details
content.value_statement: Polished interfaces are hard to judge because small motion and interaction details are easy to miss. This skill applies Emil Kowalski's design engineering principles to review UI code and guide animation choices.
actual_capabilities: Reviews UI code with a required Before, After, and Why table.
Recommends animation duration, easing, and purpose based on interaction frequency.
Guides CSS transition, transform, clip-path, and spring animation choices.
Highlights accessibility concerns for reduced motion and touch hover behavior.
Explains performance tradeoffs between CSS animations, JavaScript animation, and Framer Motion.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not automated visual testing or runtime measurement.
It focuses on frontend interaction polish and does not replace product research.
Its recommendations may need adjustment for brand, platform, or accessibility requirements.
External reference links may change outside the skill author control.

use_cases.title: Review a UI Pull Request
use_cases.description: Identify motion, easing, transform origin, and press feedback issues before a component ships.

use_cases.title: Define Motion Defaults
use_cases.description: Create consistent duration, easing, and reduced-motion rules for a design system.

use_cases.title: Polish Interactive Prototypes
use_cases.description: Refine drawers, toasts, popovers, buttons, and gestures so interactions feel responsive.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this button, tooltip, or popover interaction for polish. Return a Before, After, and Why table with concise recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Animation Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate help choosing timing and easing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose duration, easing, and trigger behavior for this UI animation. Consider frequency, purpose, accessibility, and perceived speed.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Component Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this component flow across enter, exit, hover, active, drag, and reduced-motion states. Prioritize issues that affect responsiveness and clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Motion System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create motion guidelines for our product interface. Include defaults for durations, easings, gesture behavior, reduced motion, and performance constraints.

output_examples.input: Review a dropdown animation that feels slow.
output_examples.output: A concise Before, After, and Why table that recommends faster response, stronger easing, and origin-aware scaling.

output_examples.input: Plan motion defaults for a dashboard design system.
output: Rules for when animation should be removed or reduced.
Recommended duration ranges for buttons, tooltips, popovers, drawers, and toasts.
Accessibility notes for reduced motion and touch devices.

output_examples.output: A review that covers velocity dismissal, boundary damping, pointer capture, and subtle spring behavior.

best_practices: Provide real component context, including how often users trigger the interaction.
Ask for a Before, After, and Why table when reviewing UI code.
Include accessibility and performance constraints with every animation request.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for decorative motion without explaining the user benefit.
Do not apply one timing value to every component and interaction type.
Do not ignore reduced-motion users, touch devices, or main-thread performance.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps review and improve UI motion, interaction details, component polish, and frontend animation decisions.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: It can suggest implementation patterns, but it is primarily a design engineering review and guidance skill.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The generated report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for animations?
faq.answer: No. It also covers component defaults, interaction feedback, performance, accessibility, and review format.

faq.question: Can it replace usability testing?
faq.answer: No. It improves craft and consistency, but real users should still validate important product decisions.

faq.question: Why does it use tables for reviews?
faq.answer: The skill asks for Before, After, and Why tables so design issues and fixes are easy to compare.
